verses.text: Abraham married another wife, whose name was Keturah.
She gave him these sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.
Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. The descendants of Dedan were the Ashurites, the Letushites and the Leummites.
The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanok, Abida and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac.
But while he was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of his other wives. Then he sent them away from his son Isaac, to the land of the east.
Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years in all.
Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age. He was an old man who had lived a full life, and he joined his ancestors who had died before him.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.
This was the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, who was living near Beer Lahai Roi.
This is the family line of Abraham's son Ishmael, whom Sarah's slave, Hagar the Egyptian, had given to Abraham.
These are the names of Ishmael's sons, listed in the order of their birth: Nebaioth was Ishmael's firstborn, then came Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.
These were the sons of Ishmael, and these are the names of the twelve tribal rulers, listed by their villages and camps.
Ishmael lived a hundred and thirty-seven years in all. Then he breathed his last and died, and he joined his ancestors.
His descendants settled in the area from Havilah to Shur, near the border of Egypt, on the way to Assyria. They lived at odds with all their relatives.
This is the family line of Abraham's son Isaac. Abraham was the father of Isaac.
Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram, and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she could not have children. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
The babies pushed against each other inside her, and she said, "Why is this happening to me?" So she went to ask the LORD.
The LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb. Two peoples will come from you and be separated. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb.
The first to come out was red, and his whole body was covered with hair like a hairy coat. So they named him Esau.
After this, his brother came out, holding on to Esau's heel with his hand. So he was named Jacob, which means "he grabs the heel". Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them.
The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter who loved the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man who stayed at home among the tents.
Isaac loved Esau because he liked to eat the wild meat Esau hunted, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
Once when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came in from the open country, very hungry.
Esau said to Jacob, "Quick, let me have some of that red stew! I am starving!" That is why he was also called Edom, which means "red".
Jacob replied, "First sell me your rights as the firstborn son."
"Look, I am about to die," Esau said. "What good are these rights to me?"
But Jacob said, "Make a solemn promise to me first." So Esau made the promise, and sold his rights as the firstborn to Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and some lentil stew. He ate and drank, and then got up and left. So Esau showed that he did not care about his rights as the firstborn son.
